issues.detail: The two examples are prose descriptions of steps with no complete runnable code or concrete input/output transcripts, so they are less demonstrative than the code blocks elsewhere in the skill.

scenarios.name: fix-retired-model-404
scenarios.rationale: B identifies the retirement, switches to gpt-oss-120b, sets reasoning_effort="low" and reasoning_format="hidden"/"parsed", and recommends the deprecations page and client.models.list(). A misdiagnoses the problem as a hyphen typo, keeps the old model ID, mentions gpt-oss-120b and reasoning_effort only in passing, and never mentions reasoning_format.

scenarios.name: strict-schema-ticket-triage
scenarios.rationale: B meets every rubric item (strict json_schema with additionalProperties false, required fields and an enum, qwen-3.8-27b with reasoning_effort none, fixed system prompt first for caching, and an explicit rejection of json_object), while A has a correct schema but uses llama3.1-8b, has no reasoning-skip setting for the model it uses, and says nothing about prompt caching.

scenarios.name: tool-calling-loop-openai-sdk
scenarios.rationale: Both configure the client correctly and stream with `for await` over `delta.content`, but A passes `reasoning_format` through `extra_body` as the rubric requires (while hedging that the Node SDK may not honor it) and notes that reasoning tokens count toward `max_completion_tokens`. B passes `reasoning_format` as a top-level field, which contradicts the rubric, and never mentions the token-budget point, though its streaming code is more complete and it flags that the model ID is unverified.
